name: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
alt: Duchy of Modena, Reggio and Mirandola

predecessors.name: Italian Republic (Kingdom of Italy from 1805)
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Modena and Reggio re-established when the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy was dissolved

successors.name: United Provinces of Central Italy
successors.text: 'In December, Modena joined with Tuscany and Parma to form the' United Provinces of Central Italy

ledger.x: 1814: Francis IV re-establishes the Duchy of Modena and Reggio as the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy dissolves.
December 1815: Francis IV takes the Este fiefs in Lunigiana from his mother.
17 December 1847: Guastalla passes from Parma to Modena.
1847: Fivizzano passes from Tuscany to Modena.
December 1859: Modena joins the United Provinces of Central Italy.

wars.name: Revolutions of 1831 and 1848 (Modena)
wars.outcome: The dukes 'were briefly ousted in the revolutions of 1831 and 1848, but soon returned'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Francis V 'was again forced to flee, this time permanently' (war 'April to July 1859'); Modena joined the United Provinces of Central Italy in December 1859 and Sardinia in March 1860.

certainty.note: Frontiers with Parma, Tuscany and the Papal States were fixed by the Final Act (9 June 1815) and the 1844 Treaty of Florence; Cliopatria's outlines are coarse (one H3 cell, about 250 km2, of error).
